title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
intro: This training programme equips supervisors and obliged entities to navigate the EU AML package: applying the single rulebook under the AML Regulation, the national framework under AMLD6 and AMLA's new supervisory model, and preparing for the transition.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and practitioners a clear, practical command of the EU's reformed AML/CFT framework, from the directly applicable single rulebook to AMLA's direct and indirect supervision and the strengthened tools of national supervisors and FIUs. Participants leave able to identify what changes for their institution, close gaps early and see AML/CFT controls the way a supervisor will under the new regime.
sections.What It Covers: The architecture of the EU AML package and its FATF foundations, the AML Regulation single rulebook, customer due diligence and beneficial ownership, crypto-asset service providers and the Transfer of Funds Regulation, AMLD6 and the roles of national supervisors, FIUs and central registers, AMLA's direct supervision and indirect oversight, supervisory colleges and cooperation, the interplay with restrictive measures, and readiness planning for firms and supervisors.
Intended Audience: AML/CFT supervisors, inspectors and policy staff at national competent authorities and self-regulatory bodies
MLROs, compliance officers, financial crime risk and legal staff at credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers
Senior managers and management body members accountable for the AML/CFT framework and transition planning
Learning Objectives: Explain the architecture of the EU AML package and how its Level 1 to Level 3 rulebook is built out
Apply the AML Regulation's single rulebook to policies, internal controls and the business-wide risk assessment
Assess customer due diligence, beneficial ownership and reliance arrangements against the new requirements
Evaluate the obligations on crypto-asset service providers under the AML Regulation and the Transfer of Funds Regulation
Explain AMLA's direct supervision, indirect oversight and common methodology, and the continuing roles of national supervisors and FIUs
Design a transition plan that prepares the firm or authority for the new regime
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, red-flag exercises and gap-analysis work, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors or obliged entities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purposes of money laundering or terrorist financing (AML Regulation)

Directive (EU) 2024/1640 on the mechanisms to be put in place by Member States for the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purposes of money laundering or terrorist financing (AMLD6)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1620 establishing the Authority for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AMLA Regulation)
Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets (Transfer of Funds Regulation)

modules.title: The EU AML Package: Architecture and Objectives
modules.summary: Why the EU replaced successive directives with a single rulebook and a new authority, how the package builds on the FATF standards, and how its Level 1 texts are built out through technical standards and guidelines.
objectives: Explain the weaknesses of the directive-based framework that the package addresses
Map the AML Regulation, AMLD6, the AMLA Regulation and the Transfer of Funds Regulation
Navigate the Level 2 and Level 3 measures and the phased transition
syllabus: Lessons from fragmented transposition and cross-border supervisory failures
The four legal acts and how they divide responsibilities
Regulatory and implementing technical standards, guidelines and AMLA's mandates
Application dates, transitional provisions and the influence of FATF evaluations

modules.title: The Single Rulebook: Scope, Policies and Internal Controls
modules.summary: The scope of the AML Regulation, including newly covered sectors, and its harmonised requirements for business-wide risk assessment, internal policies, compliance roles and group-wide arrangements.
objectives: Determine which entities and activities fall within the AML Regulation
Apply the requirements for business-wide risk assessment, policies and internal controls
Assess the roles of the management body, compliance manager and compliance officer
syllabus: Obliged entities, including crypto-asset service providers and newly covered sectors
Business-wide risk assessment, documented methodology and link to risk appetite
Management body accountability, compliance manager and compliance officer roles
Group-wide policies, outsourcing limits and third-country branches and subsidiaries

modules.title: Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Ownership
modules.summary: The harmonised customer due diligence regime under the AML Regulation, including simplified and enhanced measures, PEPs and high-risk third countries, and the strengthened rules for identifying beneficial owners of complex structures.
objectives: Apply harmonised CDD, ongoing monitoring and periodic review requirements
Identify beneficial owners through ownership and control, including multi-layered structures
Evaluate enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk third countries and higher-risk relationships
syllabus: CDD triggers, identification, verification and remote onboarding
Beneficial ownership thresholds, control by other means and nominee arrangements
Enhanced due diligence, PEPs and the EU lists of high-risk third countries
Reliance, outsourcing, discrepancy reporting and access to central registers

modules.title: Crypto-Asset Service Providers and the Transfer of Funds Rules
modules.summary: How the package brings crypto-asset service providers fully into the AML/CFT framework, and how the Transfer of Funds Regulation applies the travel rule to crypto-asset transfers, including those involving self-hosted wallets.
objectives: Explain the AML/CFT obligations on crypto-asset service providers and the link to MiCA authorisation
Apply the travel rule to crypto-asset transfers, including missing or incomplete information
Assess controls for self-hosted wallets, third-country counterparties and high-risk exposures
syllabus: Crypto-asset service providers as obliged entities under the AML Regulation and MiCA
Originator and beneficiary information for transfers of funds and crypto-assets
Self-hosted wallet transfers and verification of ownership or control
Correspondent relationships with third-country providers and blockchain analytics

modules.title: AMLD6: National Supervisors, FIUs and Central Registers
modules.summary: What remains with Member States under AMLD6: the powers and risk-based approach of national supervisors, strengthened FIU mandates and cooperation, and the interconnected registers of beneficial ownership and bank accounts.
objectives: Explain the minimum powers, independence and risk-based approach required of national supervisors
Describe the strengthened role of FIUs and their cooperation through AMLA
Use beneficial ownership and bank account registers as supervisory and compliance tools
syllabus: Risk-based supervision, sector risk assessments and administrative sanctions powers
FIU powers, suspension of transactions and joint analyses
Central beneficial ownership registers, verification and legitimate interest access
Bank account registers, the single access point and real estate information

modules.title: AMLA: Direct Supervision, Indirect Oversight and Methodology
modules.summary: AMLA's mandate and governance, the selection and direct supervision of high-risk cross-border obliged entities through joint supervisory teams, and its indirect oversight of national supervisors and the non-financial sector.
objectives: Explain AMLA's governance, tasks and powers
Apply the criteria and process for selection for direct supervision
Assess how AMLA's common methodology and convergence tools will change national supervision
syllabus: AMLA's General Board, Executive Board and supervisory and FIU compositions
Selection for direct supervision: cross-border activity and residual risk
Joint supervisory teams, direct supervisory powers and administrative sanctions
Common risk assessment methodology, peer reviews and oversight of national supervisors

modules.title: Supervisory Colleges, Cooperation and Sanctions Interplay
modules.summary: How AML/CFT supervisors, FIUs, prudential authorities and AMLA cooperate across borders through colleges and information exchange, and how AML/CFT controls interact with EU restrictive measures and targeted financial sanctions.
objectives: Operate AML/CFT supervisory colleges and home–host cooperation effectively
Coordinate AML/CFT findings with prudential supervisors, FIUs and resolution authorities
Assess how firms integrate targeted financial sanctions into AML/CFT controls
syllabus: AML/CFT colleges, information exchange and cooperation with prudential supervisors
AML/CFT considerations in authorisation, qualifying holdings and withdrawal
Targeted financial sanctions and screening obligations under the AML Regulation
Sanctions evasion typologies and criminal enforcement of restrictive measures

modules.title: Preparing Firms and Supervisors for the New Regime
modules.summary: Turning the package into a practical transition plan: gap analysis against the single rulebook, data and system changes, readiness for AMLA's methodology and possible selection, and the shift in supervisory expectations, ending with a planning workshop.
objectives: Conduct a structured gap analysis against the AML Regulation and emerging technical standards
Prioritise remediation of data, systems, policies and governance
Design a transition roadmap for the firm or authority
syllabus: Gap analysis: policies, CDD data, beneficial ownership and reporting
Preparing for AMLA data requests, methodology and possible direct supervision
Supervisory transition: methodologies, staffing and coordination with AMLA
Workshop: a twelve-month AML package transition roadmap

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Typologies, Tracing and Controls
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators to recognise crypto-asset crime typologies, trace funds on-chain and assess service providers' controls.

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.

related.title: Sanctions Compliance
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.
